What is corrosion mapping?

Corrosion mapping is an area thickness survey. Instead of single readings at a few points, the technician scans a defined area and records wall thickness at every position on a fine grid, tied to a fixed datum. The output is a colour C-scan plus a data file showing where the minimum wall is, how large the thinned area is, and whether the loss is general, pitting or grooving. Screening methods find where to look; ultrasonic mapping measures what is left.

Which NDT method maps which kind of corrosion

No single method finds, sizes and trends every corrosion pattern. Ultrasonic thickness is accurate but local. Screening tools cover distance quickly but report an indication, an average or a grade, not a wall thickness you can calculate with. So the usual sequence has three steps: screen to find where loss is concentrated, map the flagged areas with encoded ultrasonics, then verify the minimum before it goes to the inspector. The table shows how a Level III matches methods to the job. The "Output" column tells you whether a method gives a thickness or only a place to look.

MethodWhat it measuresOutputBest useMain limits
Manual UT thickness (dual-element probe)Wall thickness at a point or on a hand-laid gridA thickness value per pointCML readings, rough or hot surfaces, verifying a mapped minimumMisses pits between grid points; location scatter between campaigns
Encoded UT or PAUT 0° C-scanThickness at every scan position across an areaC-scan image plus an exportable thickness gridVessel shells and heads, elbows, tank shell courses, injection pointsNeeds contact and surface preparation; insulation must come off
Motorised crawler mappingSame as encoded UT, over large or elevated areasLarge C-scan mosaicsVessel shells, tank walls, long straight runsSet-up time; magnetic wheels need a steel surface and a clear path
Guided wave screeningChanges in pipe cross-section over distance from one transducer ringLocated indications, graded by severityLong runs, pipe racks, road crossings, insulated linesGives no remaining wall; range and sensitivity drop at bends, fittings and heavy coatings
Tank floor MFLFlux leakage from metal loss in floor platesIndications by plate and locationFull-floor screening during internal tank inspectionsFlagged areas need UT prove-up to get a thickness

Atlantis crews deliver UT thickness and CML surveys, encoded corrosion mapping, phased array inspection, TOFD, MT, PT, VT, eddy current, tank-floor MFL and guided-wave screening. Radiography is performed by licensed radiography crews. If your scope needs a technique outside that list, we tell you at the quote stage. All work runs under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, with ASNT-certified technicians. To scope a survey, request an inspection quote.

How a corrosion mapping test runs, step by step

A corrosion mapping test is a short sequence, not one measurement. Most of the value comes from the steps before and after the scan.

  1. Define the question. Name the credible damage mechanism (general thinning, pitting, grooving, liquid-level attack, CUI) and the code the result feeds: API 510, 570 or 653. The mechanism sets the resolution.
  2. Screen. Use visual inspection, guided wave, MFL or existing CML trends to choose where to map. Record why each area was chosen.
  3. Write the scan plan. Area boundaries, datum, scan direction, resolution, probe, couplant and temperature range, fixed in a Level III-approved procedure and technique sheet.
  4. Prepare the surface. Remove loose scale and failed coating. Sound coating can stay if the technique measures through it, such as echo-to-echo mode, and the report says so.
  5. Calibrate on the real material. Set sound velocity on a block of the same material, or on a known thickness on the component, at a similar temperature. Record a check before and after the scan.
  6. Mark the datum. Tie the area to a fixed feature such as a nozzle centreline or a weld seam, with photos, a sketch and measured offsets. This step decides whether the next survey can be compared with this one.
  7. Acquire. Scan with encoded position. Watch for coupling dropouts and lost encoder counts. Re-scan gaps before leaving the area.
  8. Check coverage. Confirm the scanned area matches the plan and that data dropouts stay within the limit the procedure sets.
  9. Analyse. Locate the minimum, the extent of the area below an agreed threshold, and the pattern of loss. Check whether low readings are true wall loss or mid-wall reflectors such as laminations, inclusions or hydrogen blistering.
  10. Verify. Prove up the minimum with a manual dual-element reading. If the pattern looks like cracking rather than thinning, flag it for angle-beam UT, PAUT or TOFD. A 0° thickness scan does not size cracks.
  11. Report and hand over. Send the C-scan, the grid file, the minimum and its location, and the datum record to your inspector of record.

Steps 1, 6 and 10 are the ones most often skipped under turnaround pressure. They are also the steps that decide whether the map is still useful in five years.

Automated corrosion mapping systems and equipment

A corrosion mapping system is more than a flaw detector. These are the parts that matter if you are deciding whether to buy, rent or hire:

  • Instrument. A UT or PAUT unit that records encoded data to a file, not one that only displays a reading.
  • Probe. Dual-element probes suit rough, pitted or hot surfaces. Linear arrays cover a wide strip in one pass. Water-column and wheel probes help keep coupling on uneven surfaces.
  • Scanner. A one-axis encoded wand suits small patches. A two-axis raster scanner suits defined areas. Magnetic crawlers suit large shells and tank walls. Chain or band scanners suit pipe circumferences.
  • Couplant feed. Usually water pumped to the probe face. Gel works for small manual areas.
  • Software. C-scan and B-scan views, thickness thresholds, and export of the thickness grid to a spreadsheet or an inspection database.
  • Reference blocks. Step wedges or blocks of matching material for velocity and zero checks.

Manual, semi-automated or automated? Manual encoded scanning suits small patches and congested nozzle areas. Semi-automated scanning, where the technician pushes an encoded scanner, covers most piping and vessel patches. Motorised crawlers earn their set-up time on large shells, tank walls and long runs. Many surveys use all three on one asset.

Buying versus hiring. The instrument is rarely the largest cost. Owners who map in-house also need technicians certified in UT and PAUT under a written practice, a Level III to approve procedures, and a way to compare data between campaigns. Atlantis trains technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III, live online or onsite at your facility. Request a training plan.

Hull and subsea corrosion mapping: what changes

Hull corrosion mapping, usually called thickness gauging, is a regulated job when it supports a ship's class survey. Classification societies accept thickness measurements from firms they have approved as service suppliers under IACS Unified Requirement Z17. On most surveys a class surveyor is involved in planning the measurements and witnessing them. Readings go into the society's own report format. The amount of gauging grows with the ship's age and the survey type. If you need class gauging, start with the approved-firm list published by your ship's class society.

Subsea corrosion mapping uses probes deployed by divers or remotely operated vehicles, often alongside cathodic protection readings. It is specialist marine work with its own qualification schemes and vessel spread.

Atlantis's mapping work covers onshore plant equipment: pressure vessels, piping, storage tanks and plant structures. The data rules in this article still apply to hull and subsea work: use a datum, set resolution for the damage, verify the minimum and keep the raw data.

US code overlay: where the numbers go

A corrosion map is evidence. The codes decide who uses it and how.

  • Pressure vessels, piping and tanks. API 510 (11th edition, 2022), API 570 (5th edition, February 2024) and API 653 (now with Addendum 4, July 2025) put the inspection programme with the owner-user. Corrosion rate, remaining life and the next inspection date are set by the owner's inspector. Atlantis delivers the NDE to your API Authorized Inspector, who stays inspector of record.
  • How to inspect. API RP 572 (vessels), API RP 574 (piping) and API RP 575 (tanks) describe inspection practice. For the ultrasonic thickness technique itself, see our note on ASME Section V Article 5 thickness measurement.
  • Process safety. For processes covered by OSHA's process safety management standard, 29 CFR 1910.119(j) expects inspection and testing to follow recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, with each inspection documented. A mapped area with a datum and a stored grid is easier to defend than spot readings.
  • Fitness-for-service. When a map shows local metal loss below the required thickness, the owner's engineer may run an assessment to API 579-1/ASME FFS-1. That assessment uses thickness profiles taken from the grid. Atlantis does not perform fitness-for-service or risk-based inspection assessments. We supply the grid in the form an assessor needs.

Canada notes. Provinces regulate pressure equipment, generally adopting CSA B51 through bodies such as ABSA in Alberta, TSSA in Ontario and Technical Safety BC. Many owner specifications ask for NDT personnel certified to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. The CGSB closed on 1 April 2026. NRCan's NDT Certification Body continues and issues CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification. Check which certification your owner specification names before mobilising.

Common mistakes in multi-method corrosion programmes

  • Treating a screening result as a thickness. Guided wave grades, MFL indications and pulsed eddy current averages tell you where to look. They are not a remaining wall.
  • Reporting the area average. Remaining life is driven by the minimum in the governing area, not the mean of the map.
  • Using a grid too coarse for the damage. A coarse grid can step right over a pit. Set resolution from the expected damage, not from the time available.
  • Mapping without a datum. Painted boundaries do not survive a turnaround. Without a datum, the next map cannot be compared with this one.
  • Ignoring temperature. Sound velocity in steel falls as temperature rises, so hot readings taken with a cold calibration read thicker than the real wall.
  • Mixing methods in one trend. A pulsed eddy current average and an ultrasonic minimum are different quantities. Trend each method against itself.
  • Keeping screenshots, not data. Without raw files and the grid export, no one can re-analyse the survey.
  • Mapping the convenient area. Low points, dead legs, injection and mix points, liquid levels and damaged insulation are where corrosion concentrates. Map them first. See corrosion under insulation inspection for the CUI side.

How to choose a corrosion mapping provider

This checklist is for integrity and QA/QC leads at refineries, chemical plants, gas plants, terminals and tank farms. Smaller plants with a few vessels can use it too. Ask each bidder:

  • Which methods will you use to screen, which to measure, and why?
  • Is the procedure approved by an ASNT Level III, and will we receive the technique sheet?
  • Are the technicians certified in UT and PAUT under a written practice to ASNT SNT-TC-1A?
  • What scan resolution will you use, and how does it match the expected damage?
  • Do we get the raw data files and a grid export, or only a PDF?
  • How will a different crew find the same area next time?
  • Who reviews the data before release, and how do urgent findings reach our Authorized Inspector during the shift?

Atlantis is based in Houston and mobilises crews to client sites. We have completed 1,500+ inspection activities, and we return a quote within 24 hours of receiving your scope. Our corrosion work links to the main corrosion mapping inspection service and the wider inspection services hub. State pages cover local codes and regulators: Texas, Louisiana and California. If you need the scan plan or the procedure reviewed before the job, talk to a Level III.

Frequently asked questions

What is a corrosion mapping test?

It is an encoded ultrasonic scan of a defined area that records wall thickness at every grid position, tied to a datum. A complete test includes the scan plan, calibration on matching material, coverage checks, verification of the minimum and a report with the grid file. It is not a single reading.

What do corrosion mapping services include?

Area selection, encoded UT or PAUT scanning, analysis and verification of the minimum, plus the deliverables in the table above. The grid file and the datum record are the two items most often left out.

What is automated corrosion mapping?

It is mapping where a motorised scanner or crawler moves the probe and records position automatically. It suits large shells, tank walls and long runs where coverage and repeatability matter. Semi-automated scanning, where the technician pushes an encoded scanner, covers most smaller areas.

What equipment is used for corrosion mapping?

An encoded UT or PAUT instrument, a dual-element or linear array probe, a scanner, a water couplant feed, software that exports the grid, and reference blocks.

Which NDT methods are best for corrosion detection?

Use screening methods to detect and locate corrosion: visual inspection, guided wave for pipe runs, MFL for tank floors and pulsed eddy current through insulation. Then use ultrasonic thickness and encoded mapping to measure what is left. Profile radiography helps on small-bore insulated lines. Eddy current suits non-ferrous exchanger tubes.

How is hull corrosion mapping different from plant corrosion mapping?

Ship hull gauging for class must be done by a firm approved by the classification society under IACS UR Z17, with surveyor involvement and the society's report format. Plant mapping on vessels, piping and tanks is governed by the owner-user's API 510, 570 or 653 programme instead.

How often should a mapped area be re-scanned?

The interval is set by your inspector under API 510, 570 or 653, based on the corrosion rate and remaining life. The map's job is to make that rate reliable. Rescanning the same area from the same datum gives a far better rate than comparing scattered spot readings.

Does Atlantis calculate remaining life from the map?

We report thickness data and, where you provide earlier data, the change between campaigns. Corrosion rate selection, remaining life and the next inspection date stay with your Authorized Inspector and engineers. For piping circuits, see piping circuit inspection and CMLs.
